question.problem:
Several children were asked their age. The age of each child (in years) was recorded below. Based on this data, if $X$ is the age of a randomly selected child, what is the standard deviation of $X?$

| Age | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of Children | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
question.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ To do this, we divide each frequency by the total, which is $1+2+3=6.$ We get the following result:

| $x$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |

Now, we compute $\text{E}[X]$ by summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =4\cdot f(4)+6\cdot f(6)+8\cdot f(8) \\  & =4(\frac{1}{6})+6(\frac{1}{3})+8(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{20}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6)+{8}^{2}\cdot f(8) \\  & =16(\frac{1}{6})+36(\frac{1}{3})+64(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{140}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{140}{3}-{(\frac{20}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{140}{3}-\frac{400}{9} \\  & =\frac{20}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{20}{9}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
